8	## General Strategy
9	
10	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
11	
12	## Recruiting Units
13	
14	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
15	
16	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
17	
18	## Promoting Units
19	
20	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
21	
22	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

70	1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
71	2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
72	3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
73	4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
74	5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
75	6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
76	7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
77	   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
78	8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
79	9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
80	10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
81	11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
82	12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

102	3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
103	4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
104	5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
105	6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
106	7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
107	8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
108	9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Lyn-mode chapters also have a **Tutorial** section: the in-game
tutorial dialogue from Normal mode, transcribed word for word, since Hard mode skips it. Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

## Lyn mode

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

| character | action                                                     |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| **wil**   | visit southwest village; otherwise he auto-joins on turn 3 |

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

| character  | action                                                                             |

| **dorcas** | **lyn talks to him** while he's an enemy; alternatively finish without killing him |

**Tutorial:**

1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns.  Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”

1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”

**Objectives:**

**Tutorial:**

1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.

### Chapter 7 — Siblings Abroad

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

**Tutorial:**

1. Starting with this chapter, you’ll be able to use the preparations screen. On this screen, you can choose who will fight, equip different items, and arrange your formation, among other things. If you have no special preparations to make, simply press START. This starts the chapter with the same group you were using at the end of the last chapter.
2. The monk Lucius has joined your group. Monks are users of the magic of light. Those who wield magic are highly attuned to its flow, so they have a high magic resistance. Units with high magic resistances can reduce the damage caused by magical attacks. When magic users battle each other, they often find it hard to inflict damage. The light magic of monks is strong against the dark magic favored by shamans. Lucius should come in handy here. Let’s put his magic to the test. Have Lucius attack the shaman nearest him.
3. It’s time to see what Nils can do. The music played by bards allows your allies to move twice in the same turn. However, bards cannot engage in combat, so be careful not to expose them to danger.
4. Through the power of Nils’s music, Lucius can move again this turn. Bards gain experience by playing music. Use Nils’s powers often, and increase his skill.
5. When you fulfill certain conditions, side quests may make themselves apparent to you. Side quests allow you to learn things that aren’t part of the main story. You might meet tough new enemies or find new companions to travel with. However, side quests are very difficult, and once you begin one, you must see it through to its end. If you plan to challenge a side quest, I suggest you keep the save data from the previous mission. Not accepting side quests will not effect your ranking. If you’re in a hurry to pursue the main story, skip the side quests.

The attack range of ballistae is extremely large, so they can fire on enemies at great distance. As they can attack without fear of counterattack, they’re quite useful. To use one, move an archer onto an unoccupied ballista, and select the ride command. After that, you can attack as usual. Ballistae can also be moved while in use. Additionally, ballistae can be used by any archer in the field. So, if you can remove the enemy manning the ballista and move one of your group onto it… you’ll find it most useful.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Lyn-mode chapters also have a **Tutorial** section: the in-game
tutorial dialogue from Normal mode, transcribed word for word, since Hard mode skips it. Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

## Lyn mode

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Objectives:**

_(filled in by the agent)_

**Recruits:**

None.

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. +- Plan for the next attempt: take the whole army WEST instead (door at (6,4), west corridor cols 0-2 south to the SW hall), so the SW group fights us and Jaffar instead of Zephiel. Verify first that the room behind (6,4) connects to the west corridor. Kill the Luna druid first (20 dmg, ignores Res).

content.text: Menu is up; choosing Restart Chapter (not Resume).
Chapter restarted from its opening narration (attempt 2). Skipping through the intro.
The restart lands on the Preparations screen this time — I can check the roster, trade items, and view the map before starting. Looking at Pick Units first.
Swapped in Pent (Sage with Physic), Lyn and Florina for Bartre, Matthew and Dart. Now redistributing items on the Preparations Trade screen.
Heaven Seal is now on Hector. I wandered into the item "List" view by mistake; backing out to finish the trades carefully.
Hector is promoting right on the Preparations screen (no turn spent). Letting the animation finish.
Hector is now a Great Lord with 17 Speed; Brave Bow going to Louise, then axes to Hawkeye.
Hawkeye now has Iron and Hand axes; moving the Hand Axe on to Hector, then Fire to Pent from the convoy.
Item setup is done (Hector promoted, weapons spread, Pent has Fire). Opening Check Map to inspect the west entrance and unit positions.

content.thinking: The west entrance turned out to be as long as the east route, so I'm going back east at full speed, with Marcus running ahead to pull Zephiel out via Rescue. I'm now opening the Formation menu to reorder the starting positions.

content.text: Marcus, Hector and Louise are now in the eastern start slots (Eliwood's slot is fixed). One more swap to bring Lyn forward, then I'll start.
Pressing Start in map view opened a minimap (confirms the layout: no shortcut to the throne room). Closing it and starting the battle from the menu.
Marcus was stopped short by the hidden Fighter in the fog (my cursor path ran through its tile), losing his attack this turn. Moving the rest up to the archway.
All units are packed at the east archway; ending turn 1 of attempt 2.
Turn 2: Marcus's counter killed the first Fighter with no damage. Rebecca lights a torch so Marcus doesn't get stopped by hidden enemies again.
Stairs cost cavalry extra movement, so Marcus stops at the top of the stairs this turn. Screening Rebecca with Hector and Hawkeye, then bringing everyone into the room.
Turn 2 ended; enemy/NPC phase is playing (Nino is trading blows with the Monk in the east). Waiting.
Turn 3: Marcus steps onto the stairs to attack the Fighter below with the Slim Lance.
Marcus killed the stair Fighter (he's 25/37). Pent tops him up with Physic now, since Marcus will soon outrun the staff's range.
Turn 3 done with the whole group at the stairs; waiting through the enemy phase.
Turn 4: Louise is in position to shoot the Mage blocking the bottom of the stairs; choosing the Brave Bow.
Hall below is clear (torch shows only a Monk by the east stairs). Marcus has dashed to the east stairs; now Hawkeye moves down and Florina will pick him up to ferry him forward.
Florina is carrying Hawkeye and everyone has filed down the stairs; ending turn 4.
Turn 5. Checking the east stairs for the Monk and what else is nearby before moving Marcus and Florina on.
Hector killed another Mage; Marcus is at the nook archway and Florina has flown Hawkeye down the east corridor. Dropping Hawkeye beside Marcus.
Everyone has moved for turn 5 (Marcus and Hawkeye are at the nook archway, the rest in the hall). Ending the turn.
Turn 6: the first Knight is beside Zephiel, same as last time. Checking the nook area before moving Marcus, Hawkeye and Florina on.
Marcus is in the central corridor; Hawkeye follows on foot and fragile Florina (10/20 HP) pulls back out of the Bishop's likely reach.
Main group is gathered at the east stairs; ending turn 6.
Turn 7. Zephiel is on his pillar with a Knight and Mage nearby. Looking south for the Bishop before moving.
Marcus and Hawkeye are forward in the central corridor as a pair; the main group is passing through Nino's nook. Finishing turn 7 moves.
Turn 7 ended; waiting through the enemy phase (Jaffar still holding the southwest).
Marcus is 35/37. Plan: Marcus takes the throne-room stair tile and Hawkeye stands right behind him, so the pair blocks the door and draws the arriving enemies instead of Zephiel.
Marcus holds the stair tile with Hawkeye beside him (Hawkeye wounded a Mercenary). Lyn has reached Nino and Talk is available — recruiting her.
Nino recruited by Lyn. Moving the last three units, then ending turn 8.
Turn 9: Zephiel is still alive on his pillar (this is the turn he died last attempt). Checking Marcus and Hawkeye at the door.
Door enemies are weak (a 6-HP Mercenary, Shamans, a Mage, and a Thief carrying a stolen Rescue staff). Hawkeye moves onto the second stair tile to seal the door and attacks the Mercenary.
The door is sealed by Hawkeye and Marcus (Mercenary killed). Bringing Hector, Louise and Pent up the corridor behind them.
Pent healed Hawkeye with Physic. Finishing turn 9 by bringing the rear (Nino, Oswin, Florina) along.
Enemy and NPC phases still playing out (Hawkeye and Marcus held the door). Waiting for turn 10.
Turn 10 reached — Zephiel survived the phase that killed him last attempt. Inspecting the door and throne room.
Zephiel is safe for now (20/20 on a pillar, one Knight left inside). Clearing the enemies outside the door: Marcus hits the Mercenary first.
Both Mercenaries at the door are dead (Marcus crit one, Hawkeye finished the other). Pent now attacks the Shaman with Fire.
All but one Knight outside the door are dead (Pent and Hector each got a kill). Bringing the lords, Nino and the rear guard up the corridor to finish turn 10.
Enemy phase: the enemies hidden inside the throne room have closed in on Zephiel. Watching the outcome.
Turn 11 — Zephiel is still alive. Checking his HP and what's around him.
Three Knights are pressing Zephiel (15/20, on a pillar). Marcus has ridden in beside them and attacks the one adjacent to Zephiel with the Steel Lance.
Marcus and Hawkeye each killed a Shaman next to Zephiel. Hector is now at the door attacking the Mage that slipped in behind them.
Hector killed the Mage. A Knight reappeared outside the door next to Louise; Pent is in range and attacks it with magic.
Pent killed the Knight at the door. Florina took Rebecca's Vulnerary and is drinking it so she can safely ferry Nino toward Jaffar next turn.
Everything has moved for turn 11 (throne room nearly cleared, Florina healed to full). Ending the turn.
Turn 12. A heavily armoured enemy has come up to the door next to Louise and Pent; inspecting it.
It's a General (38 HP, 19 Def). Pent's Elfire from two tiles away doubles for a clean kill with no counterattack.
General dead; Hector has stepped west of the door. Rebecca lights a torch so I can see the southwest hall before sending Florina and Nino toward Jaffar.
Louise killed the Mage to the west. Florina is now picking up Nino and will tuck in behind the front line.
Throne room is now clear of enemies (Marcus killed the last Shaman). Repositioning Hawkeye to the door and tidying up the rest for turn 12.
Ursula (the boss) has a dialogue event during the enemy phase. Reading through it.
Ursula's Bolting struck down Louise (she was at 16 HP), and Pent is now speaking a retreat line. Continuing to see the outcome.
Turn 13. Louise and Pent have both left the battle (Pent retreated with her). Jaffar has moved east toward us; checking the area between him and Florina/Nino.
Ursula's Bolting can kill my frailer units, so I'm walling the corridor (Hawkeye and Oswin) and having sturdy units carry the lords, while Florina takes Nino to Jaffar.
Hector is carrying Lyn; Marcus is on the stairs about to pick up Eliwood so neither lord can be targeted by Bolting.
Ursula is attacking again (enemy phase of turn 13). Advancing her dialogue to see the target.

content.thinking: Ursula is on the southwest stairs rather than the east, and Jaffar has run into the corridor west of the door with enemies after him. Hawkeye is moving to shield him or pick him up.

content.text: Rescue works on Jaffar — Hawkeye is picking him up so he can't be killed this enemy phase; Nino can talk to him next turn after he's set down.
Nino is set down on the door stairs (out of Bolting range). Florina pulls back into the throne room, then Hector steps out of Ursula's range.
It's the last turn and everyone is alive. Hawkeye will step back to the door and set Jaffar down beside Nino so she can talk to him from a tile Ursula's Bolting can't reach.
Nino is next to Jaffar and the Talk command is available — doing it now.
Nino has spoken to Jaffar. To keep him safe through the final enemy phase (he's at 18 HP), Florina will pick him up and retreat into the throne room.
"End" is highlighted — ending the final turn and watching the last enemy phase.
The chapter is won — Zephiel survived all 15 turns and the ending scene has begun. Pressing through the ending dialogue.
"Accept side quest?" appeared — the Nino/Jaffar conditions were met. The standing instruction is to always accept, so choosing Yes.
Save screen: saving to the slot already in use (the highlighted first slot).
Saved. World-map narration for the side chapter is playing; advancing to its title card.
Opening cutscene of the side chapter (Jaffar and Nino). Skipping through it to reach the Preparations screen.
